slides.title: Design for real people
slides.text: Good design starts with how real people use a thing, including people who see, hear, read or move differently.
slides.alt: Design Lab in Pro opens with a real user and their words: design starts from what people actually say.

slides.title: Edges help everyone
slides.text: A high-contrast mode made for low vision is the mode everyone uses in bright sun. Designing for people at the edges makes things better for everyone.
slides.alt: A Pro brief about designing at the edges: a mode made for low vision is the mode everyone uses in sun.

slides.title: Bias
slides.text: Bias is when technology works worse for some people because of how it was built or tested. It usually comes from who was missing from the testing group.
slides.alt: A Pro brief about bias: when a product fails some people, the testing group is the first place to look.

slides.title: Who was missing?
slides.text: Find the gap in the testing group, then widen it.
steps: face unlock fails for some skin tones
fix: test with many kinds of people
slides.alt: The last Pro brief: find who was missing from the testers, then widen the group until nobody is.

words.means: usable by people who see, hear, read or move differently
working worse for some groups because of design or testing
tools like screen readers or switches that help people use devices
the people who try a design before it is finished

slides.title: Your mission
slides.text: Open Inside the Machine at Design Lab. Fill in the audit with 4 settings, then solve 2 briefs. Base each recommendation on what the user said.
slides.alt: Design Lab in Pro opens with a real user and their words: design starts from what people actually say.
